suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-20 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline identifies paroxysmal or sustained hypertension as the most common clinical presentation of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma. Require a diagnosed pheochromocytoma (biochemically confirmed catecholamine excess with compatible imaging or histology) and separately established hypertension with compatible chronology; the cited Endocrine Society clinical practice guideline identifies paroxysmal or sustained hypertension as the most common clinical presentation of pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma, without establishing that pheochromocytoma caused an individual's sustained hypertension as opposed to paroxysmal episodes or unrelated essential hypertension. Preserve essential (primary) hypertension, renal and renovascular hypertension, other endocrine causes (primary aldosteronism, thyroid disease, Cushing syndrome), obstructive sleep apnea, medications and substances, and pre-existing hypertension antedating tumor development as competing explanations. Do not infer pheochromocytoma from episodic blood-pressure elevation or from hypertension alone, and do not treat this guideline-framed association as proof that pheochromocytoma caused an individual's hypertensive disease. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
